Method of Attack: Hooks the shutdown and reboot routines on iOS devices to fake a shutdown or reboot, preventing malware removal and allowing persistence by keeping the device operational while appearing off
Injects code into iOS daemons SpringBoard and BackBoardd to simulate shutdown indicators and intercept user input
Leverages local SSH access to gain root privileges and execute a userspace reboot that does not touch the kernel, allowing malicious code to continue running after reboot
Deceives users by displaying shutdown UI elements and Apple logo on reboot while the device remains compromised
Indicators of Compromise: Non-responsive device to user input despite appearing shut down
Spinning wheel displayed by BackBoardd daemon indicating shutdown
Apple logo effect on reboot without actual kernel restart
Simulated shutdown indicators such as dark screen, muted sounds, no vibrations, and disabled camera and 3D touch feedback
